subject: Deployment mode & data residency - follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ola Svensson <ola.svensson@nordbank.se>, Sofie Andersson <sofie.andersson@nordbank.se>, procurement@nordbank.se
Date: 2026-02-25T14:10:00-05:00
Subject: Deployment mode & data residency - follow-up and next steps

Hi Ola / Sofie / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the time today - good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery:

Summary of needs (from the call)
- Primary requirement: EU data residency for customer data (including logs and any persisted artifacts).
- Secondary: Some workloads will be latency-sensitive for EU users; a smaller subset may originate from APAC but must remain EU-resident.
- Constraint: Regulatory team is likely to require dedicated controls (audit logs, KMS integration) and may prefer a VPC or on-prem option if Hosted cannot meet guarantees.

How Redwood's deployment modes map to your needs
- Hosted API (EU region): fast to get started, regional endpoints in eu-central that keep data at rest and in transit within the EU. This is multi-tenant (shared infra) but we provide encryption, SOC2 evidence, and regional data controls. Best for non-critical/less regulated workloads and quick pilots.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools deployed to an EU region, single-tenant at the cluster level, predictable throughput and stronger isolation. Good middle ground for regulated workloads that still want managed infra.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full logical separation, customer-managed networking, optional air-gapped on-prem install. Required for the strictest regulatory cases (if your compliance team insists on customer-controlled network and keys).

Cross-region routing / residency notes
- By default, requests are routed to the nearest compatible region; however, we support tenant-level routing policies to pin a customer's traffic to a specific region (e.g., EU) to avoid cross-region egress.
- For Hosted customers we can configure an EU-only routing policy for your tenant. For the highest assurance we recommend Dedicated or Private (where you control the network boundary).

Attachments: I've attached a short PDF that compares deployment modes and a SOC2 checklist for your security team (Redwood-Deployment-Modes.pdf, SOC2-Audit-Checklist.xlsx).

Proposed next steps
1) Security deep-dive: schedule a 45-60 minute call with our security lead to run through SOC2, KMS, audit logs, and network architecture - I'll loop Vivek in.
2) Provide a pilot plan: if you prefer, we can spin a short Dedicated pilot (2-4 weeks) in the EU region to validate latency and routing controls.
3) Procurement: I can send a rough cost band for Dedicated vs Private to help procurement triage.

Do any of these next steps look good? If so, please share 2-3 times that work for a security deep-dive next week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0192

Subject: Re: Deployment mode & data residency - follow-up and next steps

Thanks Marissa - useful recap. A few quick clarifying questions from our side before we lock in the security call:

1) Hosted EU routing: when you say "tenant-level routing policy to pin to EU", does that include all persisted artifacts (logs, cached models, KV cache)? In short: can you guarantee that nothing leaves EU for that tenant?
2) Cross-region origins: some of our internal automation runs from APAC. If a request originates in APAC but is pinned to EU, is there any client-side latency or throttling we should expect (e.g., connection saturation)?
3) Dedicated vs Private: do you have a one-page comparison for compliance folks that calls out the exact controls (KMS, audit retention, network ownership)? The SOC2 checklist is good but they want a side-by-side for procurement.
4) Cost: can you give a ballpark monthly range for Dedicated (EU) vs Private VPC so procurement can triage? We don't need exact pricing yet but a 3-tier estimate helps.

If you can answer 1-3 briefly in the thread we can pre-approve attendees for the security call.

Ola
Head of Platform Security | NordBank
ola.svensson@nordbank.se

On behalf of: Procure / Security / Architecture

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ola Svensson <ola.svensson@nordbank.se>, Sofie Andersson <sofie.andersson@nordbank.se>, procurement@nordbank.se
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-02-26T09:15:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode & data residency - follow-up and next steps

Thanks, Ola - answers inline below and note I'm looping in Vivek (security lead) for the detailed call.

1) Hosted EU routing and persisted artifacts
- Tenant-level EU pinning: yes - for Hosted customers we offer a tenant-level routing policy that keeps request handling and persisted artifacts (logs, cached model shards, KV cache entries) within the EU region. We classify this as an EU-residency offering (data at rest and in transit in-region). That said, Hosted remains a shared-tenancy environment; customers who require physical isolation typically choose Dedicated or Private.

2) Cross-region origins and latency
- If a client in APAC connects to an EU-pinned tenant, traffic will traverse the network and you should expect additional egress latency proportional to geography (APAC -> EU RTT). We don't apply throttling for cross-region origins beyond standard rate limits; however, Dedicated can reduce tail latency because you control reserved GPU capacity in-region. We can run a short latency test during a pilot to quantify the impact.

3) Dedicated vs Private - summary (high level)
- Dedicated (EU): single-tenant GPU pools, predictable throughput, tenant isolation at the cluster level, full audit logs, KMS integration (customer-managed keys via our KMS connector), Redwood-managed control plane. Fast to provision compared to on-prem.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full network isolation, customer-managed VPC peering, optional on-prem installation, customer-controlled keys and hardware boundary. Recommended if your compliance team requires ownership of the network and storage boundary.

I've attached a one-page comparison as part of the Deployment Modes PDF and the SOC2 checklist we sent earlier - those should help procurement and compliance.

4) Cost bands (very high-level)
- Hosted (EU): pay-as-you-go; minimal commit - lowest entry cost.
- Dedicated (EU): ballpark starting range: mid-to-high thousands USD per month for a small reserved pool; scales with GPUs/throughput.
- Private (on-prem): higher initial setup and license/ops commitment (typically large enterprises, multi-month onboarding).

Next steps
- Vivek: can we set a 45-60 minute security deep-dive next week? Proposed slots: Wed 2026-03-04 09:00-10:00 CET, Thu 2026-03-05 14:00-15:00 CET, or Fri 2026-03-06 11:00-12:00 CET.
- Ola / Sofie / Procurement: please confirm which slot works and who will join from your side (security, architecture, procurement). We'll circulate a short pre-read (one-pager + SOC2 evidence) ahead of the call.

Thanks - looping Vivek to propose the meeting invite.

Best,
